chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Khadir al-Nakha'i

Regarding a man who has money due from another man who denies it, he said: 'If he makes him swear an oath, he is not allowed to take anything; and if he leaves him and does not make him swear, then he is upon his right.'

key_terms.اِسْتَحْلَفَهُ: he made him swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on debt recovery if the debtor denies the debt and swears an oath?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-yamin wa al-mukhallat* (oath and suspicion) in Shia jurisprudence, where the creditor's choice to demand an oath from the denying debtor serves as a final settlement of the claim. It highlights the legal weight given to the debtor's sworn testimony in the absence of other witnesses, a mechanism designed to resolve disputes through mutual consent to the oath. This reflects the practical application of evidentiary standards in early Islamic commercial law, emphasizing the creditor's strategic decision between securing a sworn denial or retaining the debt's validity.
